promise: Authored dark-fantasy campaign with fixed revelations and convergences, but no fixed player solution. Every mandatory beat has fail-forward routes.

centralTruth.publicMystery: Names are vanishing from the dead, then from records, then from living memory.
centralTruth.hiddenTruth: The Bell Beneath the World did not simply end the Siege of Orison. The Last Concord used millions of witnessed names as a metaphysical boundary, forcing the dead to remain on one side of reality. The boundary has been eroding for three centuries.
centralTruth.paleCourt: The Pale Court are identity-counterfeits formed when Bell-work preserves a pattern of a person after the original continuity is lost. Some know what they are; many do not.
centralTruth.rook: Rook is unusually resistant to name-erasure because an old Synod experiment deliberately left him partly unregistered in the Bell's memory lattice. He is not secretly a saint or chosen by blood. His importance comes from being an engineered blind spot who survived.
centralTruth.antagonistConflict: Hierophant Marlek Thorn wants to repair and centralize the Bell's control even if it requires a new mass tithe of memories. The White Widow wants the boundary to collapse so preserved identities can become fully real. Neither position is consequence-free.

mandatory.beat: Rook reaches Saint Orra's undercroft; the impossible subterranean bell is heard and the blackglass token reacts.
mandatory.failForward: If Rook avoids the morgue, a fourth erasure reaches someone nearby and forces the phenomenon into public view.

mandatory.beat: Orren Pell proves he remembers the three erased names and shows physical records where ink remains but readers slide past the names.
mandatory.reveal: Erasure is perceptual/metaphysical, not ordinary document tampering.

mandatory.beat: One corpse carries evidence of a name-transfer ritual and a reference to the Mourning Ledger.
mandatory.reveal: Someone is collecting names rather than merely destroying them.

mandatory.beat: Ysra Venn's withheld fact becomes discoverable: the first corpse was a Synod memory auditor, not a random citizen.
A path opens toward the murdered courier's blackglass memory and the wider conspiracy.
The blackglass token's last sight is decoded with help from Nereza Quill, Caedmon Voss, or an earned alternative.
mandatory.reveal: The courier saw a Pale Court transfer at a hidden archive.

mandatory.beat: Rook reaches the flooded archive and encounters evidence that several living officials have memory-perfect duplicate histories.
The White Widow becomes directly relevant but does not need to be fought.
mandatory.reveal: A counterfeit can sincerely believe it is the original.

mandatory.beat: The Mourning Ledger is recovered, copied, stolen, destroyed-but-reconstructed, or otherwise made mechanically available.
mandatory.reveal: The ledger tracks names paid into a system older than the Synod.

mandatory.beat: Evidence points simultaneously toward Greywake's old ferry compact and the Ninth Cloister's forbidden calendars.
Mara Silt confronts Rook with an old boundary bargain connected to the Bell.
A crossing requires a real cost or clever alternative; travel mechanics, salt, weather and memory magic matter.
Rook learns the Bell's influence follows old Caldran infrastructure and burial routes, not political borders.
A preserved memory reveals that the Nine Saint-Kings disagreed about the Last Concord even before it was rung.
Rook reaches the rope-less bells and forbidden calendar archives.
Caedmon Voss or a successor source decodes the Last Concord as a containment mechanism.
Bell-Keeper Edda Sol demonstrates that different bells carry different pieces of the same metaphysical command.
mandatory.reveal: Destroying one bell cannot simply end the system.

mandatory.beat: Rook discovers his own Bell-registration is deliberately incomplete.
mandatory.reveal: The Synod once created blind spots to test whether people could survive outside the Bell's full memory lattice.

mandatory.beat: Marlek Thorn's program becomes explicit: stabilize the system by collecting a controlled new tithe.
House Morcant's buried imperial road and Carrion Compact salvage converge around a functioning Bellshard Key.
Captain Iven Ash and broker Jorek Vey make competing offers around access, salvage and survival.
At least one saint-era device is activated, proving the Bell network can still rewrite what people perceive as identity continuity.
A saint-crown or equivalent command credential becomes obtainable but dangerous to use.
The Old Hart/Blackwood presents a memory system independent of the Bell: living place-memory.
Warden Halv Thornroot forces a choice between extracting a useful memory and preserving the grove's autonomy.
The Pale Court's origin is confirmed as continuity artifacts, not ordinary undead.
Rook gains enough truth to understand that repair, destruction and release each create distinct casualties.
The Bell Vault opens and all surviving interested powers converge through plausible routes.
The cost of Thorn's repair plan is made concrete: a new tithe would stabilize death but erase immense living memory.
The cost of the Widow's collapse plan is made concrete: preserved identities gain possibility at the risk of dissolving the boundary between death and memory.
Rook's incomplete registration lets him interact with the Bell in a way fully registered people cannot.

Final resolution must be earned from accumulated tools, allies, knowledge and sacrifices. Valid families include repair, destroy, release, rewrite, or an emergent fourth solution supported by campaign state.
Epilogue simulates surviving NPCs/factions/regions from actual final state rather than a fixed ending.

sideQuestlines.title: A Courier's Last Sight
sideQuestlines.hook: Decode the murdered courier's final blackglass memory.
beats: Find a safe reader of Threnody
Identify the flooded alley/archive
Learn what the courier was trying to deliver
Choose what to do with the recovered truth
sideQuestlines.reward: Unique memory ability plus evidence that can alter DM-02/DM-03.

sideQuestlines.title: Salt Debt of Greywake
sideQuestlines.hook: Mara Silt inherited a ferry bargain whose original debtor has been dead for a century.
beats: Hear the debt terms
Cross to the drowned shrine
Identify who or what still claims payment
Settle, transfer, exploit, or break the bargain
sideQuestlines.reward: Mara relationship, ferry network access, boundary ritual knowledge.

sideQuestlines.title: Ashmarket Debts
sideQuestlines.hook: Jorek Vey needs a stolen salvage charter before it is stripped and resold.
beats: Find the buyers
Trace the charter into the salvage pits
Decide ownership of the recovered imperial claim
Survive the commercial/faction fallout
sideQuestlines.reward: Salvage rights, rare materials, Jorek/Carrion reputation and alternate route to AE-01.

sideQuestlines.title: Nine Names for the Dead
sideQuestlines.hook: Orren Pell asks Rook to preserve names that are beginning to slip from him.
beats: Create redundant name records
Discover one name is deliberately false
Trace the false name to a living person
Choose which identity the burial record will protect
sideQuestlines.reward: Orren bond, funerary access, Name-Cage Reliquary path.

sideQuestlines.title: The Antler Debt
sideQuestlines.hook: Blackwood remembers a killing no human witness survived.
beats: Earn Halv's permission
Follow place-memory without treating it as infallible
Confront descendants/faction beneficiaries
Resolve whether inherited debt is legitimate
sideQuestlines.reward: Blackwood passage, living-memory technique, RR-02 leverage.
